content.value: Traditionally, security testing happened at the very end of development — right before release. Finding a critical vulnerability right before launch caused delayed releases and cost millions to fix.

**DevSecOps** moves security to the left ('Shift-Left'). Security testing happens automatically on every code commit inside the CI/CD pipeline, catching vulnerabilities within minutes while the code is fresh in the developer's mind.

content.title: Shift-Left Pipeline Security Gates
content.value:
graph LR
    A["👩‍💻 IDE Auto-Scan"] -->|git push| B["🔍 SAST Scan\n(Code Linting)"]
    B -->|npm audit| C["📦 Dependency Scan\n(Snyk/Trivy)"]
    C -->|docker build| D["🐳 Container Scan\n(Trivy CVEs)"]
    D -->|Deploy Staging| E["⚡ DAST Scan\n(OWASP ZAP)"]
    E --> F["🚀 Production"]
    style A fill:#1a2332,stroke:#10b981,color:#e2e8f0
    style B fill:#1a2332,stroke:#00d4ff,color:#e2e8f0
    style C fill:#1a2332,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#e2e8f0
    style D fill:#1a2332,stroke:#ef4444,color:#e2e8f0

**SAST (Static Application Security Testing)** — Scans raw source code without executing it (e.g. SonarQube, Semgrep).

**DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing)** — Tests a running application by sending malicious HTTP payloads (e.g. OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite).

quiz.question: What does 'Shift-Left Security' mean in DevSecOps?
options: Moving servers to the left side of the data center
Integrating automated security checks early in the development & CI/CD lifecycle rather than testing at the end
quiz.explanation: Shift-Left means moving security testing earlier in the software development lifecycle. Catching bugs at the IDE or PR stage is 100x cheaper than fixing a breach in production.

content.value: Docker base images can contain hundreds of outdated OS packages with known security flaws (CVEs). Tools like **Trivy** scan container images before deployment and block infected images from reaching production.

content.title: Scanning Docker Images with Trivy
content.value:
# Scan a local docker image for CRITICAL vulnerabilities
trivy image --severity CRITICAL,HIGH myapp:v1

# Fail CI/CD build if critical vulnerabilities are found
trivy image --exit-code 1 --severity CRITICAL myapp:v1

graph TD
    EXT["🌍 Public Internet"] -->|Explicit Auth + TLS| API["🌐 API Gateway"]
    API -->|Mutual TLS (mTLS)| SVC1["⚙️ Order Service"]
    API -->|Mutual TLS (mTLS)| SVC2["⚙️ User Service"]
    SVC1 -->|Token Validation| DB[("🗄️ Database")]
    style EXT fill:#1a2332,stroke:#ef4444,color:#e2e8f0

    style DB fill:#1a2332,stroke:#10b981,color:#e2e8f0
Zero Trust Principle: 'Never Trust, Always Verify.' Even traffic inside your internal Kubernetes cluster must be authenticated and encrypted using mTLS (mutual TLS).

quiz.question: What is the core rule of Zero Trust Architecture?
options: Never trust, always verify — authenticate and authorize every request regardless of origin
quiz.explanation: Zero Trust assumes the internal network is already hostile. Every user, device, and service-to-service call must be explicitly authenticated and authorized.

content.value: APIs are the primary gateway to your application's data. **OWASP (Open Worldwide Application Security Project)** publishes the top 10 security vulnerabilities found in modern APIs. Every cloud engineer must know how to prevent them.

content.title: Top API Vulnerabilities Cheat Sheet
content.value:
Vulnerability                       Risk Explanation & Mitigation
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
API1: BOLA (Broken Object Level Auth) User A modifies URL /api/user/102 to access User B's data.
                                    Fix: Always check token userId == URL parameter ID!
API2: Broken Authentication          Weak JWT verification or missing expiration times.
                                    Fix: Enforce strict RSA-256 JWT signature verification.
API3: Broken Object Property Level  Exposing sensitive fields (passwords/SSNs) in JSON responses.
                                    Fix: DTO sanitization — strip private fields before returning.
API4: Unrestricted Resource Consum.  Missing rate limits allows DDoS attack on database.
                                    Fix: Enforce Redis rate limiting (e.g. 100 req/min).

BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization) is the #1 most exploited API flaw in tech companies. Never trust URL parameters (e.g. GET /api/orders/55) without verifying that the logged-in user actually owns order #55.

quiz.question: What is BOLA (Broken Object Level Authorization) in API security?
options: When an API endpoint accesses a database object by ID without verifying if the requesting user owns that object
quiz.explanation: BOLA occurs when an API fails to verify whether a user is authorized to access a specific resource ID (e.g., changing the ID in the URL to view another user's invoice).

content.value: Modern applications are built like Lego blocks — 80%+ of your code comes from open-source npm/pip packages and Docker base images. **Software Supply Chain Security** ensures that third-party packages don't contain malicious backdoor code (like the infamous Log4j vulnerability).

content.title: SBOM & Supply Chain Validation
content.value:
graph LR
    A["📦 Dependencies (npm/pip)"] --> B["📋 Generate SBOM\n(Software Bill of Materials)"]
    B --> C["🔒 Sign Image with Cosign"]
    C --> D["🛡️ Kubernetes Admission Controller"]
    D -->|Verified Signature| E["🚀 Deploy to Cluster"]
    style A fill:#1a2332,stroke:#00d4ff,color:#e2e8f0
    style B fill:#1a2332,stroke:#f59e0b,color:#e2e8f0
    style C fill:#1a2332,stroke:#10b981,color:#e2e8f0

An **SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)** is an ingredients list for software. Just like a food label lists ingredients, an SBOM lists every open-source package, version, and license included in your container.

quiz.question: What is an SBOM (Software Bill of Materials)?
options: An exact ingredients list of all open-source libraries, packages, and dependencies inside your application container
quiz.explanation: An SBOM is a machine-readable inventory of software components and dependencies used in an application. It helps security teams rapidly identify if a new vulnerability affects their codebase.
